subject: COBOL words
notes: Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.2 2)` "a level-number may be the same as a paragraph-name or a section-name". Level-numbers are INTEGERLIT tokens in the data description entry and never enter the procedure table, while all-digit paragraph and section names are admitted by the procedureName definition slot. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/onetype): ex2.cob — paragraphs 01, 05 and 88 beside 01/05-level data, PERFORM 05 / PERFORM 88 -> `05 RAN 7` / `88 RAN` at 85 and 2023; ex2b.cob — `77 SECTION.`, paragraph `01.`, `05 SECTION.` containing paragraph `77.`, beside 77 N and 01 G / 05 X, with PERFORM 05 and GO TO 88 -> `05S 71` / `END` at 85 and 2023. The exception's complement (a level-number spelled like any OTHER type) is unreachable: every other type must contain a letter (§8.3.2.2) and an all-digit word lexes INTEGERLIT, so no other declaration slot can take it. REGISTER: open kb/Work PB990 lists this row in inventory_rows because its one-type census must carry this exception as data (keep it when the census lands). No spec-derived test names the exception; test-ref empty.
